steps: sin(A − B) = sin A cos B − cos A sin B.
The point of the formula is that a non-special angle is expressed through two special ones, keeping the value exact.

commonErrors.observed: Used a plus sign in the cosine addition formula.
commonErrors.likelyCause: The sign convention differs between the sine and cosine formulas.
commonErrors.remediation: Check the formula against a known case such as cos(90°) = cos(45° + 45°) = 0, which only the minus sign gives.

steps: Sine has period 360°, so adding or subtracting whole turns leaves the value unchanged.

commonErrors.observed: Treated the large angle as undefined or out of range.
commonErrors.likelyCause: The domain was assumed to stop at 360°.
commonErrors.remediation: Trigonometric functions are defined for every real angle; reduce by whole turns first.

steps: 135° lies in quadrant 2, and its reference angle is 45°.
The magnitude of the value equals the corresponding value at 45°.
In quadrant 2 sine is positive and cosine is negative.

referenceExample.prompt: Give the exact value of cos(2π/3).

commonErrors.observed: Gave the reference-angle value with the wrong sign.
commonErrors.likelyCause: The quadrant was not checked after finding the magnitude.
commonErrors.remediation: Sketch the terminal ray and read off the sign of the relevant coordinate before writing the answer.

steps: 150° is between 90° and 180°, so it lies in quadrant 2.
The reference angle is the acute angle to the nearest part of the x-axis: 180 − 150 = 30°.
So the reference angle is 30° in quadrant 2.

commonErrors.observed: Subtracted from 180° regardless of the quadrant.
commonErrors.likelyCause: One reference-angle rule was applied to every quadrant.
commonErrors.remediation: The reference angle is always measured to the x-axis; check which part of the axis is nearest.
